faq.question: What is a credit card balance transfer?
faq.answer: It's shifting your outstanding dues from one bank's card to a card from another bank, at a lower interest rate or 0% for a limited period. The new card pays the old one directly, and you repay the new card.

faq.question: Is a credit card balance transfer worth it?
faq.answer: Yes, if you're paying the revolving rate (up to 3.75% a month), you can clear the transferred amount within the offer period, and you stop adding new debt. A six-month BT on EMI can cut the cost of a ₹1 lakh balance by more than half.

faq.question: Do I lose the interest-free period after a balance transfer?
faq.answer: With a one-time balance transfer, often yes. SBI Card's terms say new purchases are charged interest from the purchase date while the transfer is outstanding. Its BT on EMI keeps the interest-free period, so check which type you're booking.

faq.question: How much can I transfer?
faq.answer: It depends on the issuer and your available limit. SBI Card allows from ₹5,000 up to 75% of your available credit limit on the receiving card.

faq.question: Does a balance transfer affect my credit score?
faq.answer: Indirectly. It uses up part of the new card's limit, raising utilisation until you repay, and missing a payment on the new card hurts your score like any other missed payment. Paying it off on time helps.
